question: Which of the following is NOT a national festival?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Diwali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Diwali** is a major Hindu festival celebrated in India, known as the Festival of Lights.
 
• It is not designated as a national festival by the government of India.
 
• National festivals in India include **Republic Day** (26th January), **Independence Day** (15th August), and **Gandhi Jayanti** (2nd October).
 
• Diwali is celebrated by millions of people across various religions, primarily Hindus, Jains, Sikhs, and some Buddhists.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Republic Day**

 
 
• Celebrated on 26th January every year in India to honor the date on which the Constitution of India came into effect in 1950.
 
• A grand parade is held in the capital, New Delhi, showcasing India's cultural diversity and military prowess.
 
 
 
• **Independence Day**
 
 
• Observed annually on 15th August to commemorate India's independence from British rule in 1947.
 
• The Prime Minister hoists the national flag at the Red Fort in Delhi and delivers a speech to the nation.
 
 
 
• **Gandhi Jayanti**
 
 
• Celebrated on 2nd October to mark the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation.
 
• The day is observed as a national holiday, and various events are organized to promote Gandhian values.
 
 
 
• **Diwali**
 
 
• Also known as Deepavali, it signifies the victory of light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance.
 
• Traditions include lighting oil lamps, bursting fireworks, and sharing sweets with family and friends.
